title: Quantization-Aware Distillation: Train the 4-bit Model, Don't Squash It
hook: Liquid AI distilled BF16 teachers straight into Q4_0 students and recovered 97% of the accuracy that post-training quantization was throwing away.
key_points: QAD distills a high-precision teacher into a quantized student, so the small model is trained rather than compressed after the fact.
Contrasts with post-training quantization (PTQ), the usual route for released GGUFs, which quantizes finished weights.
It differs from plain QAT by adding a teacher signal on top of quantization awareness.
Across four LFM2.5 sizes, 97% of the BF16 average accuracy lost to quantization is recovered.
Per-model retention: 97.1%, 96.5%, 97.4% and 96.6% of the BF16 baseline for 230M, 350M, 1.2B and 2.6B.
The Q4_0 checkpoints also decode 4–33% faster than higher-precision quantization at equivalent quality.
content_html: Small models get shipped as GGUFs, and GGUFs are usually made by post-training quantization: finish training in high precision, then squash the weights. It works, and it always costs something. Liquid AI's post makes the case for the other order — train the quantized model in the first place, with a high-precision teacher supervising.
extra_html:
How it works

Quantization-aware distillation distills a BF16 teacher into a quantized student, combining a teacher signal with quantization awareness during training. That's the difference from PTQ, which applies quantization after the fact, and the added ingredient over plain QAT, which is quantization-aware but has no teacher. The released artifacts are Q4_0 checkpoints for four LFM2.5 sizes.

Why it matters

The reported numbers are the argument: across the four models, 97% of the BF16 average accuracy that quantization would have cost is recovered, with per-model retention of 97.1%, 96.5%, 97.4% and 96.6% for the 230M, 350M, 1.2B and 2.6B variants. And because Q4_0 now holds quality that used to require more bits, the checkpoints decode 4–33% faster than higher-precision quantization at equivalent quality. For on-device deployment that's the whole ballgame — the cheapest format stops being the compromise format.

related.title: Gemma 4 QAT: 4-Bit Weights That Keep Their Quality
related.hook: Squeezing a model to 4 bits after training loses quality. Quantization-aware training bakes the rounding into training instead — and Google shipped Gemma 4 checkpoints that do exactly that.

related.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
related.hook: A big model's softened probabilities say more than hard labels - they reveal how classes relate, so training a small model to mimic them transfers knowledge a one-hot target never could.

related.title: KVarN: Variance-Normalized KV-Cache Quantization
related.hook: Long reasoning chains blow up the KV cache. Squeeze it to 2 bits and errors snowball over thousands of decode steps — unless you fix the token scales first.

flashcards.prompt: How does quantization-aware distillation differ from post-training quantization?
flashcards.back_html: PTQ quantizes weights after training is finished. QAD trains the quantized student during distillation from a high-precision teacher, so the low-precision model is learned rather than approximated.

flashcards.prompt: What does '97% of accuracy lost to quantization is recovered' mean here?

choices.text: QAD closes 97% of the gap between the PTQ checkpoint and the BF16 baseline
The QAD model reaches 97% absolute accuracy on the benchmarks
The QAD model loses 97% less throughput than BF16

flashcards.explanation_html: The figure is about the gap: per-model retention against the BF16 baseline was 97.1%, 96.5%, 97.4% and 96.6% across the four LFM2.5 sizes.

flashcards.prompt: Besides accuracy, what does the post claim for the Q4_0 QAD checkpoints?

choices.text: 4–33% higher decode throughput than higher-precision quantization at equivalent quality
Half the training compute of the BF16 teacher
Support for arbitrary bit widths at inference time

flashcards.explanation_html: Because quality at Q4_0 now matches what previously required more bits, you get the speed of the lower precision without the usual quality tax.
